label: Chaource
note: Set mainly by lactic acid (AOC: lactic coagulation of at least 12 h, slow spontaneous draining), then ripened under a white Penicillium candidum rind like a Brie

about.text: Chaource is a French cheese, originally manufactured in the village of Chaource in the Champagne-Ardenne region.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.

how.label: drain tall
how.text: The milk sets slowly, mainly by acid, so the curd is fragile and drains on its own in tall moulds. As it ripens from the rind inwards, a creamy rim forms around a fine, slightly grainy heart, with a light mushroom smell.

steps.note: Set mostly lactic, with animal rennet.

steps.name: mould
steps.note: At pH 4.75 or less, in tall moulds of 110–115 mm (450–700 g) or 85–90 mm (250–380 g), and it drains on its own.
At least 14 d in all, of which at least 8 d at 8–14 °C.
